name: Force Vortex
description: A rotating force field — a whirlpool that drags the VR player toward its glowing core, spins them around it on a tangential current, then flings them back out (outward + up) when they cross the core radius. Force as a place you're caught in, not an arrow you read. Spiral arms rotate; ground ring marks the field. Uses the proven XRToolsPlayerBody.velocity launch path, applied continuously. DNA: field_radius, pull_strength, spin_strength, lift, eject_radius, eject_force, eject_up.
theoreticalGrounding: A force field assigns a velocity to every point in space. Here v_in = -r̂·pull + (ŷ×r)·spin (inward + swirl); cross the core and v_out = r̂·eject + ŷ·up. Centripetal in, centrifugal out — felt in the body.

force_vortex.name: Force Vortex
force_vortex.description: Rotating whirlpool force field. An Area3D (cylinder, player_body layer) captures the player; each physics frame the field overwrites their velocity with inward pull + tangential spin + gentle lift, spiralling them toward the core; crossing eject_radius throws them outward + up, then a cooldown. Rotating spiral arms + glowing core + boundary ring. DNA: field_radius (3.5), pull/spin/lift, eject_force/up.
force_vortex.qfep_connection: F_force: a field is a velocity per point — pulled in, spun, thrown out; the body rides the vector current.

dna.default: depiction=spiral, warning=none - together these ARE the shipped vortex. spiral is the `_:` branch of the match and computes the same arithmetic line for line (3 arms, 14 beads, t*TAU*1.1, radius lerpf(0.25, field_radius*0.98, t), height 0.15+t*1.2, size lerpf(0.12,0.04,t), colour field_color->core_color, energy lerpf(3.2,1.4,t)); only the four lines that instance the bead moved into _bead(). warning=none returns on the first line of _build_warning and builds no node at all. Neither key is passed by any existing placement - force_vortex is named in 11 map files (Force_Preview, VFM_Field, VFM_04_Fields, Zone_WarehouseLab, Zone_WarehouseLab_Packed and six museum trials) and every one of them renders byte-identically. apply_grid_config is now guarded: it used to free every child and re-enter _ready() on ANY call, and now rebuilds only when a value actually differs AND the first build has happened.
dna.was: eight @export knobs and every one a magnitude - field_radius, pull_strength, spin_strength, lift, eject_radius, eject_force, eject_up, cooldown_time. Turning them made the same whirlpool pull harder or throw further; not one of them was a claim, and the throw itself is an event no still can hold. The drawing - three arms, fourteen beads, 1.1 turns, a 1.2 m rise - was hard-coded in the body of _build_field with nothing able to reach it. The runner refused the token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS, which was a fact about the kind of knob.
dna.note: depiction is WHAT A FORCE FIELD IS DRAWN AS, with the law held fixed: every value applies the identical v_in = -r-hat*pull + (y-hat x r)*spin + y-hat*lift and the identical throw, and lays the identical bead - same taper, same gradient, same emission falloff - in a different arrangement. spiral is a current you can see before you are in it; spokes is the textbook arrow picture, the inward pull drawn honestly and the swirl not drawn at all; rings is level sets, where you are and never which way you are going; funnel is the rubber-sheet well, gravity's metaphor imported into a vortex with no mass in it; column puts every bead on the boundary, a field as a room you are inside. NOT named `field` although vector_field_grid declares an axis by that word - those five values are five different laws the plane obeys, these five are one law drawn five ways, and the distinction is the whole point. warning is reused character for character from path_block (which took it from catalyst_vent): how much the object tells you BEFORE it costs you anything. It fits here because eject_radius is 0.9 m and the shipped drawing marks it NOWHERE - the core column is 0.22 m of cylinder and the floor ring is the outer boundary, so the circle where the field stops pulling and starts throwing you is invisible. That is a true statement about the artifact, so it is the default. Both axes are appearance-only: the Area3D, the capture cylinder and the throw are identical at every value, because a field you cannot see is not a weaker field.
dna.declines: pull_strength / spin_strength / lift / eject_force / eject_up / cooldown_time stay plain numeric exports - a faster spiral is a rate, and the evidence here is one still per value.
